comparison: Perfect agreement on intestinal colonization, tissue damage, and inflammatory responses (C3-C5, C34-C38, C41-C42, C45). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by qPCR, histopathology, and RT-qPCR data. Reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'Leptospira infection was able to cause intestine damage and inflammation.'

Perfect agreement on therapeutic synergy between LPS neutralization and pathogen-directed therapies (C17-C18, C94-C103). Both evaluations strongly support these findings. Reviewers state the combination 'significantly improved the survival rates' and describe it as 'a potential new therapeutic approach.'

Perfect agreement on negative culture results (C63). Both evaluations support this finding as important for distinguishing intestinal translocation from systemic bacteremia. OpenEval notes the limitation that only two culture conditions were tested.

Perfect agreement on antibiotic-induced bacterial lysis and Jarisch-Herxheimer-like effects (C170-C171). Both evaluations support these findings as providing mechanistic insight into why antibiotic monotherapy is insufficient.

Strong agreement on increased intestinal permeability and tight junction changes (C7-C8, C57-C59). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval includes additional claim C139 not mentioned in peer review. Reviewers explicitly state 'increased gut barrier permeability' as a key result.

Strong agreement on microbiota's causal role demonstrated by antibiotic depletion and FMT rescue (C11-C13, C69-C71, C73-C74, C146-C147). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval covers broader claim set including antibiotic depletion details (C64-C68) addressed separately in peer R5.

Agreement on IL-10 findings (C75-C76). Both evaluations support that IL-10 levels did not differ between microbiota-manipulated groups, contrasting with TNF-α and IL-1β. Peer review groups this with other negative findings (C54).

Agreement on bacterial translocation demonstrated by FISH (C9, C61-C62). OpenEval also includes LPS elevation claims (C10, C82) which peer review addresses in same result. Both evaluations accept the FISH methodology and findings without concerns.

OpenEval addresses LPS elevation in serum (C10, C82) while peer review groups this with bacterial translocation findings. Both evaluations support the LAL assay data and the gut-derived source of LPS.

Partial agreement on microbiota alterations. OpenEval comprehensively covers all microbiota sequencing claims (C6, C46-C54) while peer review focuses on key findings (C6, C52-C53) about Proteobacteria expansion. Both evaluations support the 16S rRNA sequencing approach.

OpenEval's comprehensive microbiota analysis (C46-C54) overlaps with peer review's acceptance of temporal dynamics (C46-C51, C125). Both evaluations support the biphasic pattern of diversity changes. Peer review emphasizes the unbiased nature of omics methods.

Agreement on gut-derived inflammatory mediators and macrophage responses (C14-C15, C84-C85, C89). Both evaluations support the in vitro stimulation experiments. OpenEval includes additional mechanistic claims (C86-C88) and notes lack of controls for confounding factors.

Agreement on polymyxin B neutralization of LPS-mediated inflammation (C16, C91-C92). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes that claim C93 ('essential' role) is somewhat overstated, while peer review accepts the mechanistic interpretation.

OpenEval addresses PMB neutralization data (C93) while peer review groups this with broader interpretive conclusions about clinical implications. OpenEval rates C93 as SUPPORTED but notes overstatement; peer review accepts the mechanistic model.

OpenEval specifically evaluates antibiotic depletion and FMT restoration data (C64-C68, C151-C153) while peer review groups these with broader microbiota manipulation findings. Both evaluations support the experimental approach and partial restoration by FMT.

Agreement that interpretive and speculative claims (C115-C116, C121, C123-C124, C131, C133, C138, C142-C143, C154, C157-C158, C174, C181) are UNCERTAIN. Both evaluations recognize these as inferences requiring further validation. Editor notes work 'could be dissected further in future studies.'

OpenEval rates clinical application claims (C173, C177-C178) as UNCERTAIN speculations requiring human studies, while peer review SUPPORTS the interpretive conclusion about clinical implications. Reviewers state work has 'potentially important clinical implications.'

Agreement on route-dependent disease kinetics (C36, C107). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval groups with survival data while peer review addresses methodological observations about infection routes.
OpenEval addresses route comparison (C36) as part of intestinal colonization findings, while peer review primarily focuses on core pathology findings. Both evaluations support C36 without concerns.

OpenEval supports biphasic tight junction response and Claudin-2/diarrhea link (C144-C145) while peer review groups C145 with other interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN. Slight divergence in confidence about mechanistic interpretation.

Agreement that background/contextual claims about leptospirosis (C1-C2, C19-C25) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Both evaluations treat these as established literature providing necessary context.
Agreement that background claims about microbiota-pathogen interactions (C26-C29, C31-C33) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Both evaluations accept these as establishing study rationale.
Agreement that background claims about barrier function and LPS (C55-C56, C77-C81) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Both evaluations accept these as providing mechanistic context.

Agreement that background claims about inflammatory responses and TLR signaling (C39-C40, C90, C159-C160, C164-C166) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Both evaluations accept these as contextualizing the findings.

Agreement that background claims about barrier dysfunction and therapeutic precedents (C60, C140-C141, C167-C169) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Both evaluations accept these as providing context for the therapeutic approach.

Agreement that methodological and background claims (C155-C156, C172, C175-C176, C179-C180, C182-C184) are SUPPORTED. Both evaluations accept the justification for using female hamsters and other methodological choices.

Agreement that discussion claims contextualizing findings within existing literature (C104-C106, C108-C109, C114, C118-C119, C122, C126-C127, C129-C130, C134, C137, C148-C149) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations and comparisons.
OpenEval addresses discussion claim C106 about route comparisons while peer review groups route-related findings (C106-C107, C110-C113) together. Both evaluations support these observations.

OpenEval supports observational claims C30 and C72 about clinical manifestations and cytokine effects, while peer review groups C30 with extensive background claims. Both evaluations accept these without challenge.

OpenEval rates claims about colonization independence from route (C111-C112) as UNCERTAIN inferences, while peer review SUPPORTS these as methodological observations. Divergence in interpretation of what is directly demonstrated versus inferred.
